neighbours.label: untrue or invented stories: the word that marks a story as fabricated ('tall' tales, 'fairy' tales, 'tell a' lie, 'tells' lies)
fire: Around the campfire, Grandpa told tall tales about wrestling a bear.
The children begged their mother to read them one more fairy tale.
If you tell a lie to your doctor, you only hurt yourself.
He was known in the village as a man who spins yarns about his travels.
Most legends grew up the same way fairy tales do, passed from mouth to mouth.
Politicians who tell lies on camera are rarely punished for it.
The sailor loved to tell outrageous stories that nobody believed.
She made up a fib about losing her homework on the bus.
quiet: Around the campfire, Grandpa told true stories about his years in the army.
The children begged their mother to read them one more chapter of history.
If you tell the truth to your doctor, you get better treatment.
He was known in the village as a man who writes letters about his travels.
Most news reports are checked by editors before they are printed.
Politicians who tell the truth on camera are often praised for it.
The sailor loved to describe the ports he had visited in detail.
She wrote a note about losing her homework on the bus.

notes: Card: ' fairy' x10, ' tall' x2 (tall tales), ' telling' x2, 'tell a lie', 'a person who tells lies', Washington Irving's folktales. Logit on + pole suppresses tall/fib/yarn, so this pole promotes them. Near misses keep storytelling but the stories are true or factual.
